### Keep the stable job, take the creative risk on the side (Naoufal Fillali)
Cite as: [Source: "Naoufal Fillali: Keep the stable job, take the creative risk on the side"]
Principle: Earn your living in a career where outcomes are spread fairly evenly, and place your creative bets in the winner-take-all domain only with money and time you can afford to lose.
- He sorts careers into two kinds, following Taleb: ones where pay tracks effort and the top earns a small multiple of the average (dentist, accountant, sales), and ones where one outlier takes almost everything (author, athlete, YouTuber). Creators usually live in the second kind. [2:21 to 4:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LO5tAzkcEeY&t=141s)
- The advice to quit and follow your passion reaches you through survivorship bias: the creators who failed rarely post about it. [0:46 to 1:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LO5tAzkcEeY&t=46s)
- His own answer is a barbell: a tech sales career as the safe side, videos and writing as the speculative side, funded by savings he can afford to lose so money never bends the work. [5:46 to 7:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2PnIP39miSs&t=346s)
- He points to people who worked this way, Kafka in insurance, Einstein as a patent clerk, Spinoza grinding lenses, Taleb writing after trading, and to Bertrand Russell's case for a modest day job that protects a writer's freedom. [5:43 to 6:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qmab27g1zcY&t=343s)
- His schedule makes it concrete: reading and research for about two hours before work, the day job from nine to six, filming and editing in the evenings, longer blocks on weekends. [5:45 to 6:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LO5tAzkcEeY&t=345s)
- A day job also feeds the work: contact with colleagues and ordinary problems makes creative output more relatable, as Kafka's insurance years shaped The Trial. [8:50 to 9:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LO5tAzkcEeY&t=530s)
- Without money pressure, creative work can stay play; he argues financial stress turns it into anxious hit or miss projects. [9:36 to 10:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LO5tAzkcEeY&t=576s)
- A serial barbell is another option: build skill and reputation in a safe profession, then make the leap with the old profession to fall back on. [7:33 to 8:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dUxG43_po5s&t=453s)
- He applies the same logic to athletes: extreme winner-take-all pay, tiny odds, and injuries that can end everything make a pro sports career one of the worst bets even for the talented. [0:45 to 4:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6MaVLhX3RaI&t=45s)

### Find out which of your desires are borrowed (Naoufal Fillali)
Cite as: [Source: "Naoufal Fillali: Find out which of your desires are borrowed"]
Principle: Most wants are copied from the people around us; name the models you imitate, choose better ones, and make time alone to find the desires that are actually yours.
- Drawing on René Girard and Luke Burgis, he explains that we mostly want things because people we watch want them, and that this runs below awareness. [1:34 to 2:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyF1ewvwsiQ&t=94s)
- He separates distant models (celebrities we admire) from close ones (friends, classmates, neighbors we compare ourselves to); the close ones steer career picks and purchases most. [1:57 to 3:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyF1ewvwsiQ&t=117s)
- He saw it in college, where peers chose finance mainly because everyone rated it highly and later disliked the work. [1:57 to 2:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FoSfma9I80E&t=117s)
- Envy can be used as a signal: notice whom you envy, and if it is for learning, courage, or independence rather than watches and lifestyles, let that point you toward better models. [2:42 to 3:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FoSfma9I80E&t=162s)
- Thin desires come from conditioning and leave you empty once reached; thick desires hold up. He went to Norway for several days without screens or music, journaling and walking, to sort one from the other. [6:42 to 8:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyF1ewvwsiQ&t=402s)
- Four habits he uses against copied taste: read old books, value things at what they are worth rather than what branding claims, keep anti-models you do not want to become, and do not be contrarian just for the sake of it. [11:31 to 14:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FoSfma9I80E&t=691s)
- Raw preferences show up through solitude and a lot of trial and error with cities, books, and hobbies; being mainstream where you genuinely agree is fine. [14:09 to 14:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FoSfma9I80E&t=849s)
- The same trap follows money: people move up, compare themselves with richer neighbors, and chase income to impress rather than to buy freedom. [13:20 to 14:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dUxG43_po5s&t=800s)
- In his view a simple life is harder than a sophisticated one, because it means questioning what advertisers and peers have taught you to want. [13:12 to 14:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2PnIP39miSs&t=792s)
- As a manager he found most team conflict came from people wanting the same thing, and prevented it with clear territories and responsibilities. [4:43 to 5:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyF1ewvwsiQ&t=283s)

### Read old books, carry one everywhere, keep an anti-library (Naoufal Fillali)
Cite as: [Source: "Naoufal Fillali: Read old books, carry one everywhere, keep an anti-library"]
Principle: Reading is a habit you build in downtime, deepen by going broad and deep, and filter by time: books that have survived centuries are the best bet.
- He disliked books until his early twenties and later realized he did not hate reading, only being told what to read. [1:55 to 2:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YkLTZyCae2I&t=115s) and [5:04 to 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YkLTZyCae2I&t=304s)
- He started with a floor of ten pages a day and always kept a book or audiobook with him, reading in the dead minutes that would otherwise go to scrolling; that got him through about twenty books the first year. [3:54 to 5:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YkLTZyCae2I&t=234s)
- Reading was tied to a concrete goal, getting an opportunity to move from Morocco to Paris, and he credits it with helping him land the internship. [2:42 to 3:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YkLTZyCae2I&t=162s)
